title: Geometric regularity of a formal fibre ascends along a map quasi-finite at the prime
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to R'$ be a ring map of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] making $R'$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Let $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak p'$ be prime ideals of $R'$ and $\mathfrak q=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')\subseteq\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')$. Assume that $R\to R'$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak p'$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] (affine case, Stacks Algebra Definition 00PL), i.e. the prime of the fibre ring $R'\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p'$ is an isolated point of its spectrum. For a prime $\mathfrak s$ of a Noetherian ring $T$ write $\kappa(\mathfrak s)=T_{\mathfrak s}/\mathfrak sT_{\mathfrak s}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $(T_{\mathfrak s})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nT_{\mathfrak s}/\mathfrak s^nT_{\mathfrak s}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. If the $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-algebra $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then the $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$-algebra $(R'_{\mathfrak p'})^\wedge\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), item (1), and its proof (Algebra Lemma 07NC lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime; Algebra Lemma 0381 for the base field extension)

proof.text: (Splitting the completed base change.) Put $S=R'$, $\mathfrak q_S=\mathfrak p'$; then $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\mathfrak p$, $R$ is Noetherian, $R'$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra and $R\to R'$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak p'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime] there are a ring $B$ and a ring map $\beta$ such that $(\phi,\beta):(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RR'\to(R'_{\mathfrak p'})^\wedge\times B$ is a ring isomorphism, where $\phi(x\otimes y)=\hat\varphi(x)\iota(y)$ is the natural map. Make $B$ an $R'$-algebra via $y\mapsto\beta(1\otimes y)$ and $(R'_{\mathfrak p'})^\wedge$ via the canonical map $\iota:R'\to R'_{\mathfrak p'}\to(R'_{\mathfrak p'})^\wedge$; then $(\phi,\beta)$ is an isomorphism of $R'$-algebras, since $\phi(1\otimes y)=\iota(y)$. (Stacks: $R'_{\mathfrak p'}\to(R'_{\mathfrak p'})^\wedge$ is a factor of a base change of $R_{\mathfrak p}\to(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite), proof of (1), first display (Algebra Lemma Tag 07NC)

proof.text: (Tensoring with $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$.) Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $k'=\kappa(\mathfrak q')$, $F=(R'_{\mathfrak p'})^\wedge\otimes_{R'}k'$ and $B'=B\otimes_{R'}k'$. Applying $-\otimes_{R'}k'$ to the $R'$-algebra isomorphism of the previous step, and using that $-\otimes_{R'}k'$ commutes with finite products ($(X\times Y)\otimes_{R'}k'\cong(X\otimes_{R'}k')\times(Y\otimes_{R'}k')$, the tensor product being additive and the product of two modules their direct sum, compatibly with the multiplications), gives an isomorphism of $k'$-algebras $((R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RR')\otimes_{R'}k'\cong F\times B'$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite), proof of (1), 'It follows that ... is a factor of'

proof.text: (Rewriting the left side.) Since $\mathfrak q=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$, $\varphi$ maps $R\setminus\mathfrak q$ into $R'\setminus\mathfrak q'$, so it induces a local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak q}\to R'_{\mathfrak q'}$ and a field map $k\to k'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and the structure map $R\to R'\to k'$ equals $R\to k\to k'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] for $R\to R'$ with the $R'$-algebra $k'$ and the $R$-algebra $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ (together with the symmetry $X\otimes Y\cong Y\otimes X$), $((R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RR')\otimes_{R'}k'\cong k'\otimes_{R'}(R'\otimes_R(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge)\cong k'\otimes_R(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ as $k'$-algebras; by the same lemma for $R\to k$ with the $k$-algebra $k'$, $k'\otimes_k(k\otimes_R(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge)\cong k'\otimes_R(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ as $k'$-algebras. With $A=(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_Rk$, the $k$-algebra of the hypothesis, this gives an isomorphism of $k'$-algebras $C:=k'\otimes_kA\cong F\times B'$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite), proof of (1), second display $R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_RR'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak q')=R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak q)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\kappa(\mathfrak q')$

proof.text: ($k'/k$ is finitely generated.) Let $y_1,\dots,y_n$ generate $R'$ as an $R$-algebra. Every element of $k'=\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is $\bar a/\bar s$ with $a\in R'$, $s\in R'\setminus\mathfrak q'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $a,s$ are polynomials in the $y_i$ with coefficients in $R$, whose images lie in $k$; hence $k'=k(\bar y_1,\dots,\bar y_n)$ is a finitely generated field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite), proof of (1) (implicit: needed for the base field extension of Algebra Lemma Tag 0381)

proof.text: (Extension of the base field preserves geometric regularity.) By hypothesis $A$ is a Noetherian $k$-algebra, geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Let $L/k'$ be either $L=k'$ or a finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then $L\otimes_{k'}C=L\otimes_{k'}(k'\otimes_kA)\cong L\otimes_kA$ as $L$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change], and $L$ is a finitely generated field extension of $k$ [def-pc-field-extension] (generated by $\bar y_1,\dots,\bar y_n$ of the previous step and a finite $k'$-basis of $L$). By [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] (Algebra Lemma Tag 0381, (2)$\Rightarrow$(1)) $L\otimes_kA$ is Noetherian and regular. With $L=k'$: $C$ is a regular, in particular Noetherian, ring; with $L$ finite purely inseparable: $L\otimes_{k'}C$ is regular. So $C$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k'$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite), proof of (1), last sentence: 'extension of base field preserves geometric regularity, see Algebra, Lemma 0381'

proof.text: (Passing to the factor.) Let $L$ be $k'$ or a finite purely inseparable extension of $k'$. By the isomorphism of step 3 and since $L\otimes_{k'}-$ commutes with finite products, $L\otimes_{k'}C\cong(L\otimes_{k'}F)\times(L\otimes_{k'}B')$ as rings, and the latter is regular by the previous step. The projection $\pi:(L\otimes_{k'}F)\times(L\otimes_{k'}B')\to L\otimes_{k'}F$ is a localization at the multiplicative subset $M=\{(1,1),(1,0)\}$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring]: $\pi(1,0)=1$ is a unit, every element of $L\otimes_{k'}F$ is $\pi(f,0)$, and $\pi(f,b)=0$ means $f=0$, so $(1,0)\cdot(f,b)=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring] $L\otimes_{k'}F$ is a regular ring. With $L=k'$ this shows that $F$ is Noetherian (and regular); with $L$ finite purely inseparable it shows that $L\otimes_{k'}F$ is regular. Hence $F=(R'_{\mathfrak p'})^\wedge\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ is a Noetherian $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$-algebra which is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks 07PP(1) (agrees; q, p are the contractions of q', p'). Proof follows the Stacks proof of (1) in six steps: the 07NC splitting R_p^ (x)_R R' = (R'_{p'})^ x B (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, stated with the natural first projection as in the 'sanity check' of the Stacks proof, so the splitting is one of R'-algebras), tensoring with kappa(q') (finite products, elementary), rewriting the left side as kappa(q') (x)_{kappa(q)} (R_p^ (x)_R kappa(q)) by lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change twice, kappa(q')/kappa(q) finitely generated (elementary), base field extension preserves geometric regularity written out from lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions (Stacks cites Algebra 0381 for this), and passage to the factor written out via the factor being a localization at the idempotent (lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring). Mathlib searches of the item (three kinds, 2026-10-10) kept: no match.
